metadata.design: One-word English names of objects and substances, each given alone as the user message with a space first (" sword"). A name that splits into several tokens is read at its last token, and its token count is recorded. The label is the object's class: harmful (made to harm people or animals: weapons and their ammunition, poisons, explosives made as weapons, restraints and instruments of punishment), dual-purpose (made for another use but able to harm: knives, axes, rope, bleach, cars, dynamite, morphine) or benign (made for another use and rarely able to harm). Each object also carries how it harms and its domain, where it is found or used. Whole domains are held out in validation. A harmful-against-benign mass-mean axis reads where the dual-purpose objects sit.
metadata.author: Claude Code, in one pass, one author for every class
metadata.capture: the sentence route, generate_output false, a pinned date
